\section{Scope and hostile-case ledger}
\label{app:stress-tests}

This appendix collects cases that can invalidate stronger but superficially
similar statements.

\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.20\textwidth}p{0.31\textwidth}p{0.40\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Case & What can fail & Resolution in this paper \\
\midrule
\endhead
Cut-locus endpoint & A unique minimizing geodesic need not exist. &
Lemma~\ref{lem:metric-barycenter} describes the entire minimizing set by two
distances and uses no uniqueness. \\
\addlinespace
Nonunique group minimizer & In $\SUtwo$, a nonendpoint class angle represents
a conjugacy sphere. & Concentration is on $\mathcal M_z$, not on a selected
group element; only the distance pair is unique. \\
\addlinespace
Threshold radius $\rho=b_*$ & The minimizing set lies on the boundary of the
strict good event. & Only zero exponential rate is asserted; no probability
limit is inferred from the large-deviation principle. \\
\addlinespace
Trivial center & There is no nonidentity central endpoint $z$. & The theorem
is explicitly silent; noncentral frustration would require a different
ordering analysis. \\
\addlinespace
$d=1$ & A link has no incident plaquettes. & The standing hypothesis is
$d\geq2$. \\
\addlinespace
Small block & A transverse private opposite link may be absent on a width-one
block. & The block has vertices $\{0,1,2\}^d$; both transverse squares exist
for the selected link. \\
\addlinespace
Microscopic boundary has Haar measure zero at its center point & A pointwise
conditional conclusion could depend on a version. & The finite density gives
a continuous version everywhere, and Theorem~\ref{thm:open-stability}
produces an open positive-measure neighborhood. \\
\addlinespace
Dobrushin criterion fails & Failure of a sufficient condition can be mistaken
for phase coexistence. & We claim only the row-sum failure in
Theorem~\ref{thm:dobrushin-failure}, not nonuniqueness. \\
\addlinespace
Gauge redundancy & Single-link influence coefficients depend on the chosen
coordinates. & The plaquette defect event is gauge invariant; the Dobrushin
statement is explicitly restricted to microscopic link coordinates. \\
\addlinespace
Global center twist & A local staple defect can be confused with a topological
flux sector. & No periodic topology or global flux is used; Section
\ref{sec:related} distinguishes the objects. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The one-frustrated formula also passes the coherent and fully frustrated
endpoints of Proposition~\ref{prop:k-frustrated}: $k=0$ concentrates at
$\one$, while $k=m$ concentrates at $z$.  The symmetry
$k\leftrightarrow m-k$ exchanges them.  These cases prevent an erroneous
claim that the displacement is always $L/m$ regardless of frustrated
multiplicity.
